17	
18	Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query is the headless, integer-only simulation record of every light in the world (the chest beam, ship fixtures, machinery lanterns, thrown glowsticks, alarm beacons and fault glows) plus the one question it answers: how much of that light reaches a registered point, and is it enough to work by. Read this GDD if you design or build anything that must ask "is this lit" (Interaction's lit-only verbs, Attention's light stimulus, Horror Entities, Suit's beam charge, 2D Lighting's drawn edge, Derelict Authoring's lamps): it fixes the emitter records and their commands and mutators, the shape table, the lamp, glowstick, beacon and fault-glow formulas, the cone and occlusion tests, the hysteresis, the caps and the acceptance criteria, and it never reads a `Light2D`, a physics space or a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
19	
20	**Two `lit`s, kept verbatim (EM-2):** the *record field* `emitter.state.lit` means an emitter is emitting (`output_pm > 0`, true for any kind and read by the Presenter on the seat's beam); the *query* `lit(ref)` means a registered subject's exposure is above the technical-artist's threshold with hysteresis (`LIT_ON_PM` 150 / `LIT_OFF_PM` 120). Neither is ever renamed.
21	
22	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` (systems-index enumeration row 5, Recommended Design Order 7; Category Core) · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer`, `Life-Support Graph`, `Player Controller & Input`, Layout, Item & Module Database, Suit & Equipment, Ship Body (all designed; the counterparts that were undesigned at first draft — Layout, Suit, Ship Body, Interaction, 2D Lighting, Attention, Horror, Derelict Authoring — are now Status Designed, so the contracts below are two-sided and an item still tagged provisional waits on a counterpart's text, not on a missing GDD) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Depended on by 6 systems on the index's graph (2D Lighting & Occlusion, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Derelict Authoring, Attention, Horror Entities), and read without an index edge by Web Map & Transit (hard: E1 at `init_world`, E10, `lit` for the pod console), Failure & Trail, Adaptive Audio & Tells and the HUD & Suit Layer (soft; Open Question 15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
23	
24	## Overview
25	
26	Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query is the simulation's record of every light in the world and the one question it answers about them: *how much of that light reaches this point, and is it enough to work by?* In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `emitter.state`, that holds an **emitter record** for each chest beam, ship fixture, machinery lantern, thrown glowstick, alarm beacon and fault glow, written only through commands and published mutators, plus a pure **exposure query** that combines those records with the Layout's opaque footprints into a per-subject `lux_pm` (0..1000) and a `lit` bit. It is the data layer under three things the player feels directly: the edge of their own lamp (what the lamp reaches is exactly what they can read and touch), the dimming of a ship lamp when the scrubber draws, and the way the web answers to light (Attention, Horror Entities and the act-only-on-lit rule all read the same answers). It never reads a `Light2D`, never touches a physics space, never obtains a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view, and runs identically headless, on the host and under test.
27	
28	The player never operates an emitter table. They meet it as a **pool of light with an edge**. The chest lamp (hands-free, Pandorum-style, origin at the per-facing chest point, `|x| <= 2` px) lays a wedge across the deck; a valve wheel half inside it prompts exactly when the wheel's anchor crosses the drawn edge and not a pixel sooner; the corridor lamps sag when the tier browns out and the junction box at the rim of their pool loses its prompt; a glowstick thrown into the next room blooms Chemlight green, holds steady, and then visibly shrinks; a lamp switched on takes a handful of ticks to warm because the ship has to serve it first. Nothing is ever shown as an exposure readout of any shape, or a "visibility" number (P3: shown in the world, never as a hidden meter): the only gameplay surface of the whole system is a prompt that is present or absent, drawn by the HUD, and the world itself.
29	
30	The block exists because three decisions already made elsewhere need one honest place to live. The index (TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY) split *emitter state* from *light rendering* so that light is a simulation input no hallucination can touch (kernel CR-12) and so that Attention can run headless and on the host for remote players. The Controller made the beam an emitter "like any other for Attention" and made every verb act only on a lit object (PC-5, PC-6), which demands one query that the prompt, the `validate` step and the channel re-check all call. The Graph made lamps ordinary LOADs whose brightness is `base * served_pm / 1000` (registry formula `power_allocation`), which demands a place that turns that served power into a light a subject can be inside of. The result is a bottleneck with six dependents (2D Lighting & Occlusion, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Derelict Authoring, Attention, Horror Entities).
31	
32	**What the game loses without it.** There is no honest "go dark" strategy (nothing for Attention to read), no lit-only rule (PC-6 has no query to call), no way for a lamp to be dimmer because the ship is starved (P1: "a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served"), no stable edge for the Tell's filaments to resolve at (P2), and no sim-side truth for Lighting to conform to, so the first hallucination that bends a cone would be indistinguishable from a bug. The sim/render agreement that this block guarantees by construction (the drawn hard edge *is* the queried edge for a full-output emitter) is the load-bearing P1 test of the whole lighting stack.
33	
34	**Index wording, reconciled.** The index (rationale bullet 5) describes a geometric light-exposure query made of a cone test plus occluder tests on physics shapes. This GDD honours the substance, the Layout's collision footprint rectangles as the occluding shapes, and changes the means: occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test against those same rectangles behind an `OccluderSource` seam, with no physics backend in the MVP (EM-20). The reason is the index's own intent — the block "runs headless" and lets Attention run headless and on the host (kernel H10; CR-13 G3: the 2D physics engine makes no determinism claim, so a physics-derived `lit` flowing into a persisted block would have to be recorded for replay). The index and kernel wording refresh this implies is routed in Cross-References. Index numbering, once and for all: this system is **enumeration row 5**, rationale bullet 5, **Recommended Design Order 7**.
35	
36	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): the `OccluderSource` seam and the integer segment test (ADR candidate 1); the subject-registration model with static and dynamic layers and counted work units (ADR candidate 2); the fixed-point direction table and Q28 cone test with zero floats on the sim path (ADR candidate 3); the broadphase (uniform grid versus room-gated) and whether the spatial index lives in Layout or here (ADR candidate 4); the occlusion-origin rule, contingent on the Lighting spike (ADR candidate 5). No ADR exists yet (`docs/architecture/` holds only `tr-registry.yaml`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The review adds to candidate 1 the **cell convention** of D.6 (cells as unit squares, doubled coordinates), to candidate 4 the **static-rebuild policy** (D.14 scenarios; synchronous, with the per-pair cache and the narrowing of door-leaf invalidation) and the (b) alternative it rejects, and a new candidate 6, the **read-view storage layout** (EM-25: typed or packed columns, sorted subject columns, a per-tick snapshot). Under workflow tier `full` these six ADRs are written with `/architecture-decision` before story breakdown, and the inline rulings and "alternatives considered" text then move into them (Open Question 24).*
37	
38	## Player Fantasy
39	
40	**Framing: indirect, with a cost layer.** The player experiences this system as the edge of their own light and the prompts that live inside it; they never see "exposure", an "emitter" or a "query". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A "The Honest Edge" adopted as the headline, with Framing C "Light as a Spend" as its price. Framing B "Lamp Management" — brightness dials, shape switching, lamp banks as a resource panel — was rejected: it breeds an exposure readout, which P3 forbids, and a shape-change input, which PC-5 forbids. Logged.)*
41	
42	> The lamp is on your chest. It is the only light that follows you, and it is the only way to touch anything: what is not in the light cannot be worked (the four exceptions of the registry `act_gate` aside: `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument and `throw_glowstick`, and the ACTOR_SELF self-patch, an actor verb on the player's own suit (Interaction IA-6)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Every fixture on the home-ship, every running machine's lantern, every glowstick you leave behind is the same bargain. Light lets you read the ship, and light lets the web read you.
43	>
44	> Competence is choosing light, not having more of it. A veteran crew does not carry a brighter lamp; they know which corridor lamp to kill before a sortie, where a glowstick buys the most room for the least time, and when a second of beam on a dark corner is worth what it shows.
45	>
46	> And the edge never lies. Eyes can be wrong about what stands in the light, but not about where the light ends. When the sanity goes, the dark may fill with shapes and the cone may seem to reach further than it does; walk to the edge and it is exactly where it always was, and nothing past it will answer your hand.
47	
48	**The emotion named: the bargain of sight** — agency purchased with exposure, under a guarantee that the light itself is never the liar. The power is not dominance over the dark; it is the small, honest sovereignty of your own light: you choose where the edge of the known world is, and the edge is where you left it.
49	
50	**Tone and language.** Use: *lamp, chest lamp, beam, in the light, the edge, go dark, the lamp warms, the pool shrinks, spend light.* Avoid meter words (*visibility, detection, stealth, hidden, light level, lux*; `lux_pm` is an internal name and is never player-facing) and avoid *flashlight* (it implies a hand-held tool; the lamp is chest-mounted) and *torch* for the beam (the anti-pillars use "torches" for the VS-A deployables; concept Pillar 1's "carries their torch" means the beam, a wording refresh owed to the concept, listed in Cross-References). The ludonarrative anchor is the user's decision of 2026-10-26: the lamp is on the player's chest, hands-free, like Pandorum. The player *is* the lantern, so going dark is not putting a tool down; it is hiding your own body.
51	
52	**Anchor moment (solo; the MVP is single-player).** Derelict A, power dead. The hatch opens on black. You thumb the chest lamp on: the click comes first, the light a breath later (PC-5: the sound pre-plays, the light follows committed state). A wedge of your wide beam — 30° half-angle, 288 px / 6 tiles, placeholder rows of the art bible 8.3 table — lays a hard edge across the deck plates. At the far end of it, half in, half out, a valve wheel. You turn a hair to the left and the wheel's prompt appears at the same moment the wheel does; a hair back and both are gone. The edge is a fact. The next compartment is past a bulkhead your beam cannot bend around. You crack a glowstick and throw it (Interaction's throw, `THROW_RANGE_TILES` 3). Chemlight green (#86B896) blooms in a room you have not entered yet, a 2-tile pool (96 px, an Item DB placeholder) that will not flicker but will shrink. Now there are two lights in this derelict and only one of them follows you. Something creaks overhead; filaments are resolving at the rim of your cone (Attention's presentation). You switch the lamp off. The dark is honest: the valve still exists, you just cannot touch it now. Behind you the glowstick you left keeps burning. You chose to leave it. It is still lit, and it is still yours to answer for.
53	
54	**Second beat (home-ship, Graph-coupled).** Back aboard, the scrubber spins up and the corridor lamps sag as the power tier browns out (`lamp_output_pm` = `base * served_pm / 1000`). The pool under the galley lamp pulls in; the junction box at the edge of it, which you could reach a minute ago, is now outside the light and has no prompt. Nobody told you the power is short. The light told you. *(The crewmate beats — a downed crewmate's beam as a locator in the dark, a saner crewmate's beam as the truth check — are Vertical Slice B (VS-B); the MVP fantasy rests on the honesty of your own edge.)*
55	
56	**Pillar alignment.** *Pillar 1 (primary), verbatim:* "Three channels are inviolable ... The human channel. Voice/proximity chat and a crewmate's own light beam (colour and shape) are never faked." And the art bible's Principle 1 anchor: "The physical radius your light actually reveals is a fixed anchor and never lies. Even at low sanity, the hallucination layer may add things but may not move that boundary." This block is that anchor in the simulation: the edge the player sees is the edge the query answers. *Pillar 3 (primary), verbatim:* "The players' light, noise, power use and restraint raise or lower its attention ... shown in the world, never as a hidden meter ... Restraint and stealth are real strategies." Every emitter is exposure; off-screen emitters still expose; going dark is a real, measured choice. *Pillar 4:* "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust." The true edge is a falsifier that costs a step and the exposure of standing in your own beam. *Pillar 2 (supporting):* the Tell's signature image, filaments resolving at the cone edge, needs a stable edge to resolve at. *Pillar 5 is not served* (glowstick scarcity is Suit's and the Item DB's). The "spend light" cost layer leans on glowstick scarcity, which is P5-adjacent (scarcity pushes inward), so the spend has a named economic owner and is not an unanchored promise: **the scarcity-to-depth link is routed to the Item & Module Database and Suit & Equipment** (the Item DB's `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` and its salvage-only faucet, Suit's per-seat carry and start counts, and Derelict Authoring's loose-stick supply by depth); this GDD prices the light (a stick is a real, shrinking reveal radius and a real exposure) and owns none of the supply.
57	
58	**Design tests.**
59	1. **The honest edge (system test).** *When the place you can act differs from the place you can see light vs. they coincide → they coincide.* At rest (aim committed, not sweeping), an object whose anchor is one base pixel inside the drawn hard edge of a single full-output hard-edged emitter is in the light and prompts; one pixel outside is not and does not. This is the sim/render agreement test (a `(spike)` until Lighting exists). It holds for a *full-output* emitter; a dimmed emitter's actionable area honestly shrinks (see Formulas, `EDGE_FLOOR_PM`).
60	2. **Light is the price of agency.** *When a choice lets the player act without light vs. requires light to act → require light.* (the registry `act_gate` exemptions, four: `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument and `throw_glowstick`; plus the ACTOR_SELF actor-verb rows, i.e. the self-patch (Interaction IA-6, which is not an object exception); the first draft listed three) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* Otherwise working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy.
61	3. **Light is never free.** *When a choice makes a light safe (unseen by the web, no cost) vs. keeps every emitter an exposure → exposure.* Corollary: off-screen emitters still expose; a glowstick you walked away from is still yours to answer for.
62	4. **The lie draws, it does not reach.** *When a hallucination could change what is actionable vs. only what is drawn → only what is drawn.* No Filter output changes `emitter.state` or any query answer.
63	
64	**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Light gets the same split the Graph drew for the physical world. The left column is what this GDD guarantees by construction (a `SIM`-only block, kernel CR-12, EM-29); the right is what the Perception Filter and Lighting may do, as presentation only.
65	
66	| Cannot lie (truth channel — this GDD guarantees) | Can lie (presentation — a decoy overlay drawn by Lighting on mask bit 3 from the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, LO-21) |
67	|---|---|
68	| The true reveal edge of every emitter: reach, cone, occlusion | Decoy lights that are not emitters (not in `emitter.state`, expose nothing) |
69	| Beam colour and shape, including a crewmate's (VS-B) | Shadows with no occluder (stage-2 drift, art bible 4.4) |
70	| Lamp and fixture brightness as served (`lamp_output_pm`) | A decoy glow appears past the true edge (an overlay, leaking violet) |
71	| Whether an object is in the light (`lit(subject)`), and therefore whether it prompts and accepts verbs | A decoy overlay that may itself flicker, on the decoy mask bit (Lighting; flash-clamped) |
72	| Glowstick waning: a real, monotone shrinking of the reveal radius | What a lit object looks like (the module-body channel: sprite, gauge) |
73	| Exposure to the web | — |
74	
75	**The falsifier this hands the player.** A phantom extension of the cone carries no prompts and accepts no verbs, because the query never answered "in the light" there. So the cheapest truth check in the game needs no instrument: *reach for it.* If it is real light, the prompt is there. Cost: a step forward, a second, and the exposure of standing in your own beam. The ladder, cheapest first: (1) reach for it; (2) walk to the edge; (3) drop a glowstick (a second light, a second witness); (4) a saner crewmate's beam (VS-B, the human channel); (5) time. **Required leak:** any drawn extension past the true edge must carry the sane-palette leak (violet or flesh fringe at the false region — art bible 4.4, "subtle is allowed; absent is not"). That is a requirement this GDD states on Lighting and the Perception Filter, not something it implements. **Dependency of the falsifier (flag, routed):** "reach for it" holds only if no system ever draws a prompt where the query says not in the light — phantom salvage targets (kernel Open Question 14, Interaction's) and HUD prompt drawing must route through `lit(subject)` and nothing else. If a phantom target could prompt inside a decoy region the cheapest falsifier dies. An unregistered ref therefore answers exactly like an unlit one (EM-21); Interaction owns the ruling on phantom targets. *Art-bible wording tension (routed, not a value conflict):* art bible 4.4 lists "the cone seems to reach further than it does" as stage-2 drift, while Principle 1 names the true light radius an anchor that never shifts. They reconcile exactly as above — the *drawn* cone may be extended by a decoy; the *revealing* radius (what is actionable, what the query answers) does not move — and the art bible should say "a decoy glow appears past the true edge" so nobody reads it as licence to move the boundary.
76	
77	**Reference techniques, taken precisely.** *Pandorum* — a chest-mounted, hands-free lamp that swings with the body (*adopt*, user decision); the hand-held torch traded against tools (*reject*: the hand point is a lightless grip, PC-5). *Project Zomboid* — lit houses seen from outside draw the horde (*adopt*: fixtures expose even when nobody is near; off-screen emitters count); the flashlight as a battery item (*adopt*, but the charge is Suit's). *Alien: Isolation* — your own light gives you away and turning it off is a tactic (*adopt*); the motion tracker as a threat readout (*reject*: no readout of any shape). *Darkwood* — the vision cone as the boundary of the known (*adopt*); the cone as a mask that hides drawn geometry (*reject*: art bible Principle 1, unlit not fogged, real occlusion). *Monaco* — line of sight as the honest rule of what you know (*adopt*: real occluders make "a shadow with no occluder" a readable lie). *Lethal Company* — a crewmate's flashlight as their locator (*adopt for VS-B*). *Amnesia / Don't Starve* — darkness drains sanity or kills (*reject*: darkness here is honest and is the *safe* choice; light is the cost; routed to Sanity so go-dark stays a valid strategy). *Doom 3* — flashlight or weapon (*reject*: no weapon exists to trade against). *Thief / Splinter Cell* — a light gem or any visibility readout (*reject*).
78	
79	**What each emitter kind means to the player** (the tone table Lighting and Audio read; the numbers stay with their owners).
80	
81	| Kind | Player meaning | Feel rule (presentation owner) | Numbers owned by |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| BEAM (chest lamp) | "My light; me." | Snaps on: the click pre-plays, the light lands on commit. Never dims for drama. A dim pool at the feet (the spill, EM-6) shows what is underfoot and nothing more. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Art bible 8.3 rows, placeholders (confirmed by the Lighting spike) |
84	| FIXTURE (ship lamp) | "The ship's light; it costs the ship." | Warms on across the switch latency, sags under brownout, never flickers (the cryo-bay gutter is Lighting's). | Art bible 8.3 / Item DB `emits` |
85	| FIXTURE, subkind DOCK_STATUS (the pod's status glow) | "The way home is still on." | A small, dim, steady glow on the docked pod at the dock room, on while the pod is parked at that dock (switched by Web Map's `pod_at` write, E10), independent of the ship's power; it is a lamp like any other, so it also shows the web where you came in (EM-11). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Derelict Authoring placement, art-director luminance (kept apart from the visible-unknown lamp), `DOCK_STATUS_*` knobs *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
86	| NODE_LANTERN | "That machine is alive, and it is shining." | No switch: it shines because the machine runs. Killing the machine is the only way to dark it. | Item DB `emits` |
87	| GLOWSTICK | "A light I left behind." | Steady, never flickers, shrinks honestly; its waning is the only clock, read in the world with no timer. | Item DB `GLOWSTICK_*` placeholders |
88	| BEACON | "The one light nobody chose." | A rotating sweep, an alarm owned by Attention's breach machine. | Art bible 8.3, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` |
89	| FAULT_GLOW | "The failure lights its own repair, and the web sees it too." | Ember, arc and cyan mist as point sources. | Failure & Trail's descriptor-to-glow table |
90	| (VS-A) flare / torch / decoy | "A light I spend to buy time." | Flicker is Lighting's; the query uses the steady mean. They repel or distract; they never harm. | Suit / Item DB |
91	
92	**A focused searchlight is louder (deliberate).** The light stimulus Attention reads is output times reach (D.12) and is blind to the beam's shape, so the narrow beam (reach 384, the one that reveals the least of a room) reads about 2.3 times louder than the fan (reach 168). That is the intended trade, not an accident of the formula: a tight, far-reaching searchlight is a bright, far-carrying thing to be, and the loadout choice is *reach and focus against being heard by the web*, not a free pick of the quietest cone. No per-shape weight column exists in the MVP. *Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D25).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
93	
94	**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails).**
95	1. **No exposure readout of any shape.** No gauge, gem, icon, overlay, light-level number or "visibility" text in gameplay. The only gameplay surface is a prompt that is present or absent. The Debug Overlay (`DIAGNOSTIC`) may draw cones, segments and subject exposure and is absent from release.
96	2. **The beam reveals; it never repels or harms.** No beam stuns, burns, repels or damages a horror or a crewmate (rejected: the Alan Wake light-as-weapon pattern; anti-pillar "not a combat game"). Horrors may read exposure (`lux`, `emitters_near`) to decide behaviour (`lit_by` is deferred to VS-A, EM-24) — that is Horror Entities' — and being revealed is the beam's whole effect. VS-A flares, torches and decoys may repel or distract (anti-pillar "tools may repel"); that behaviour is Horror's and is never a damage channel. *(Horror Entities is now designed and re-runs this GDD's no-occluder, no-emission criterion as AC-HE-67; status refreshed 2026-10-27 — design review.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
97	3. **No light progression.** No beam upgrades, brightness levels or unlocks. Shape is a Suit loadout fact; better light comes from salvage, if at all.
98	4. **No mid-run shape switching and no brightness dial.** On and off is the only beam choice.
99	5. **Shining a beam on a crewmate has no mechanical effect** (anti-PvP): it does not blind, mark or harm; in VS-B it is only a truth check.
100	6. **Fixtures are placed by welding sections, never freeform** (anti-builder). No player-placed lamps in the MVP; glowsticks are the only player-placed light, and they are consumed.
101	7. **No stealth score or "hidden" status.** Going dark lowers a stimulus Attention reads; nothing tells the player they are hidden.
102	8. **Darkness is never punished by this system.** It neither drains, damages nor penalises; the dark only withholds agency (you cannot act on what is unlit). Any sanity cost of darkness is a **hard constraint on the Sanity & Hallucination Rules GDD, not a warning** (creative-director, CD-GDD-ALIGN: darkness never costs sanity, because go-dark collapses as a strategy, and P3's restraint with it, if darkness costs more than the exposure it saves; Open Question 4).
103	9. **No light for free.** No ambient reveal radius around the player; the avatar is a light source only through its beam. The one near-field exception is the beam's own foot pool (`BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` 24, EM-6): it exists only while the beam is on, is drawn, and reaches 24 px from the feet, so an object underfoot is not a broken prompt. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). Walls east or west of the avatar cost at most the 4 px of chest-x offset. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The cone's apex, reach and distance are therefore measured from the chest, while the occluder segment to a subject starts at the foot origin (`pos_curr`, `beam_pose`). Other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What ships for each Lighting-spike outcome** (2D Lighting LO-10; its spike step 3b is a **pre-implementation gate for ADR candidate 5**, not a later check): outcome **B** (the light's `offset` moves the apex without moving the shadow origin) — the foot-origin rule ships as written and Lighting draws the shadow from the foot; outcome **A** (the shadow originates at the chest) with AC-57 passing — the foot-origin rule ships and the residual discrepancy (≤ 2 base px) is recorded; outcome A with AC-57 failing (a beam that renders black, or leaks through the wall, while the sim reports the opposite) — outcome **D** ships: ADR 5 adopts the walk-back (the sim occludes from the chest, walked back to the first clear point on the segment to the foot), D.4, EM-20 g and AC-10 are re-derived, and nothing else in this GDD changes. Until the spike reports, the foot-origin rule is the working rule and the worst case — a beam that renders black while the sim reports it lit, which would happen every time a player walks up to a wall — is an open risk (Open Question 5). **Near-field is aim-dependent, and the ruled answer is a drawn foot pool, not a control tax** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ruled 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D24)*: an object between the lamp and the feet in screen-y is behind the apex when the player faces up-screen; the cone is honest about it (nothing in the drawn cone reaches it either) and the sim adds no hidden compensation. The first draft called this "a skill expression"; the systems-designer, endorsed by the creative-director, reads it as a **control tax caused by the chest-lamp decision**: an object at the player's feet, or one tile to the side, is dark in every shape in any unlit room even though it is inside Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72, and it will read as a broken prompt, not as horror. P1 is preserved if the spill is *drawn*; the price is a small loss of P3 darkness right at the body. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions):** `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` ships at **24 px** (range 0–48; 0 switches the spill off) with `BEAM_SPILL_PM` 600 registered, as a dim, drawn, honest pool that gates actions only within its own actionable radius `r_lit_px` of the feet (18 px at the defaults, D.7 chain) and contributes minimally to exposure; Interaction's `REACH_PX` 72 is a different, larger distance (the hand's reach) and the spill does not light everything inside it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it is validated by the *dark-at-feet* metric of the first playtest (the playtest stub's placeholder decision line is 5 % of lit-beam ticks; Open Question 17). The user's chest-lamp decision stands unchanged: the lamp is still on the chest and still the only light that follows the player; the spill is a small, honest, drawn pool at the feet. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The mechanics were fixed ahead of the ruling so that the ruling is one data value: the spill is one extra SOFT, omnidirectional, non-shadow contribution of the BEAM record, centred on the foot origin (`occ_origin`), of reach `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` and output `BEAM_SPILL_PM` (600, range 150–1000, owner game-designer; registered), present only while the beam is on (the beam record's `switch_on`, so the spill flips with the beam and adds no transition of its own to the commit-spacing guard), tested with the ordinary radius, occlusion and clearance rules, added to the `act_lux_pm` and `lux_pm` of objects (never to the owner's ACTOR self-lux, EM-21) and **excluded from `section_emission`** (D.12 counts the beam's cone term alone, so the spill adds no Attention load). At 24 px and 600 permille its actionable radius `r_lit_px` is **18 px, read from the D.7 integer chain** (the retired closed form ⌊24 × 450 / 600⌋ agrees at this one point and is not used; at d = 18, f = ⌊1000 × 6 / 24⌋ = 250 and c = ⌊600 × 250 / 1000⌋ = 150 = `LIT_ON_PM`; at d = 19, f = 208 and c = 124 < 150): it covers an object at the feet and not one a full tile (48 px) to the side; **no legal setting reaches a full tile**: at the maximum radius 48 and the maximum output 1000 the chain gives `r_lit_px` 40 (at d = 40, f = 166 and c = 166; at d = 41, f = 145 and c = 145), so "48 px to the side" is dark by design at every value in range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Subject kinds it applies to:** every registered subject kind except the owner's own ACTOR (EM-21 keeps the owner's self-lux at the beam's apex value): OBJECT, ITEM, a second seat's ACTOR (VS-B) and HORROR, each through the ordinary radius, occlusion and clearance rules; a horror within the spill's radius of the player's feet therefore reads lit (`lux_pm` up to 600), which is honest exposure and is not a special case (AC-10c). **The spill is published to Lighting** through the read-view accessor `beam_spill(beam_id)` (EM-26), not through `emitters()`, so that the sim edge and the drawn edge can be proved equal and so that Attention's list never counts it. It is `light_shape` row 11 `BEAM_SPILL` (a registry entry this GDD owns; see EM-8): a **conditional** row, present in the shape table iff `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0, and it needs a Lighting texture and AC-10b. A non-zero radius must also satisfy I-REACH (at least `REACH_MIN_PX` 24), so the effective range is 0 (off) or 24–48. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

169	**EM-7 — The beam changes only on committed state.** `toggle_beam` is owned by Emitter State and fixed by the Controller (PC-5, PC-2): `actor` = the seat's beam emitter id, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source = emitter.state` (kernel CR-7: the authority check keys `(emitter.state, beam_id)`, so a beam id never matches a Body actor id or a deployable's emitter id held under another key) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, origin `PLAYER`. The payload carries no state (it is a toggle: the `beam_toggle` press flips `switch_on`), so a rejected or duplicated command can never desynchronise the intent. Its apply flips `switch_on` in P2 of tick T; `emitter.place` in P3 of the same tick computes `output_pm`; the committed light therefore changes in the tick the toggle applies, with zero internal latency. The click and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately (Presenter); **the light changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts beam state** (PC-5), because the beam is the human-channel anchor and may never lie, not even for one flicker. The seat's beam id is allocated by E9 inside the new-game LOADING (the Emitter's `init_world` step, or the session owner's new-game step under the same `WriteScope`, before the kernel's rebuild); the Emitter registers a **kernel binding source** at BOOTING (kernel CR-7): `beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`, a pure read of `emitter.state`; the kernel's LOADING rebuild binds each pair after every `post_restore()` (new game included), which is what lets `toggle_beam` carry `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. The binding table is not saved (CR-7) and is rebuilt from `beam_bindings()` after every restore (EM-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *Alternative considered:* the Controller allocates the beam id — rejected (CR-8). **Strobe protection is a sim guard, owned here** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; this supersedes the first-draft orchestrator ruling that routed the whole concern to the Controller's Adapter)*: the Adapter's debounce (`BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS`, owner Player Controller & Input, registry, PC-5) covers only the local human submitter, and PC-5 and Controller Open Question 18 both state that the sim-side guard "is Emitter State's to add"; with no guard here a replayed, scripted or remote submitter bypasses it and Suit SE-35's drain-sampling protection (the six-tick window) and the WCAG 2.3.1 limit rest on one client. The validate order is `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY`. An Adapter-compliant stream is never rejected **only if** `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` is at least `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`: the Adapter's registry value is 10 today, so until the Player Controller raises it to 12 (its range 10–20 allows it; 2D Lighting Ask E-E proposes the same) a human stream pressing every 10 ticks has every second press refused `TOO_SOON` (no light change, no charge drain); this is listed under I-SPACING (D.15) and AC-90b, not hidden. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

The projected commit tick is the apply tick `T_a` for an OFF that would darken a lit or armed lamp, and `arm_tick` of D.2 for an ON (a deterministic function of `T_a`, EM-12). Rules: (1) an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels an ON that never became visible and is never refused (it is not a realised transition, EM-12, AC-80); (2) the guard measures *realised switch transitions only*: a brownout, a node failure or `served_pm` falling to 0 changes `output_pm` but is the world's doing, not the submitter's, and writes nothing; (3) the guard applies to `PLAYER` and `SYSTEM` origin alike; the MVP has **two `SYSTEM` submitters in this area and neither is a `set_switch` submitter**: Attention's breach machine submits `set_beacon` (which carries no per-emitter guard, below) and Web Map & Transit switches the DOCK_STATUS glow through the guard-free mutator E10, so a refused `COOLDOWN` is only ever seen by the `PLAYER` path at the MVP (the `SYSTEM` form of `set_switch` is kept for VS-A, where a submitter receives `COOLDOWN` like anyone and may resubmit on a later tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (4) a same-state `SYSTEM` `set_switch` is accepted and changes nothing (below) and is not a transition; (5) `toggle_beam` keeps its domain code `TOO_SOON` (the Controller's tests and AC-90 name it), `set_switch` uses `COOLDOWN`; both are this GDD's codes under `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`. **Consequence for the player's tap path** (stated so that no one assumes Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 covers it): the tap guard spaces *submissions* by 12 ticks, while this guard spaces *commits*, and an ON commits at `arm_tick`, up to 5 ticks after its apply; so an ON tapped at tick 1201 (commit 1206) followed by an OFF tapped at 1213 (the first tap `TAP_REARM_TICKS` allows) commits at 1213, only 7 ticks after 1206, and is refused `COOLDOWN` until a tap that commits at 1218 or later (12 after 1206, subject to Interaction's own re-arm). Fixture flips are now bounded here by the commit-spacing guard above (every origin), in addition to Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` (IA-21, registry, which keeps the *submission* rate) and the Graph pulse that delays every switch-ON (EM-12); `set_beacon` carries no per-emitter guard here and Attention's breach machine, its only submitter, rate-limits itself (the residual of Open Question 25). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

208	Rows 9 and 10 are new numbers (not in the art bible 8.3 table): *placeholder, owner technical-artist / Failure & Trail, confirmed by the Lighting spike*. Row 11 is new and **conditional**: it exists in the shape table iff `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` > 0 (default 24, user ruling D24, 2026-10-27), is owned by the game-designer and art-director, and is validated by the dark-at-feet playtest metric (EM-6, Open Question 17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* `COS2_Q28` is the square of the Q14 cosine of `half_angle_units`, in Q28 (EM-19). The split's axis is 206 units, not the 205 that 18° rounds to, because with the cones' half-angle rounded to 114 units a 205-unit axis leaves a 182-unit (15.996°) wedge and fails the art bible's "dark wedge ≥ 16°" (invariant I-WEDGE, Formulas D.15). The split's axes are ±206 units off the committed **aim**, not off facing (an art-bible wording refresh, Cross-References). The beam's `output_pm` is the constant `BEAM_BASE_PM` while on (placeholder 1000, owner game-designer; no low-charge dimming in the MVP). Reach and output of every shape row are independent of depth in the web and of Attention level: the art bible fixes the revealing radius as the one physical anchor, so "the dark presses in" is presentation (Lighting's ambient) and never a reach change (Open Question 3, resolved 2026-10-27: user ruling, kept). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
209	
210	**EM-9 — The beam in every actionable state; DOWNED keeps it, DEAD ends it.** The beam is available while the actor is IDLE, WALK, RUN, CARRY_WALK or CHANNELLING (PC-8; the user's chest-lamp decision: nothing the hands do touches the lamp). While `loco_state == DOWNED` the beam keeps its committed state — the aim is frozen at the last committed value and the origin is the `chest_sim` of the down animation row; a downed crewmate is a locator (P1) — which is the handoff PC left to this GDD ("Emitter State decides what a downed emitter does"). While STAGGERED the state is likewise unchanged. At the tick `emitter.place` reads `loco_state == DEAD`, it forces `switch_on` false (the Controller's `DEAD` row: "beam off (Emitter State on actor death)") as an `emitter.place`-internal `force_off`, a read of `controller.state` with no command. Because Save/Load's death stub restarts from the last autosave through `request_restore` at that tick's P6, the DEAD-tick off-state is unobservable in the MVP (say so in tests). A beam that stays on over a corpse until Suit's charge runs out — a corpse as a lantern the web can see — is *not* a rule here; it is a VS-B question for Attention and Sanity (Open Questions). In IN_POD the beam follows its actor into the pod's body frame (EM-30; Ship Body's `body_of_actor` carries the frame and Web Map & Transit is designed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
211	
212	**EM-10 — Beam charge is Suit's.** Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD "beam and tool charge" reading (art bible HUD set). `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge (the strobe floor `TOO_SOON` of EM-7 applies to both directions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Suit's divisor-6 `suit.vitals` reads `emitter.state.lit` on the seat's beam to drain charge and calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5) at zero; because `suit.vitals` runs earlier in the tick than `emitter.place`, a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's `emitter.place`, and the owner's six-tick re-check (EM-25) then finds a channelled target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target. The beam is a *suit load, not a ship LOAD*: Emitter State never calls `set_load_request` for it and the Graph is not involved. (Suit & Equipment, designed: SE-8; Suit keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`.)
213	
214	**EM-11 — Fixtures are switchable Graph LOADs; the lamp formula gates on the switch.** A FIXTURE carries `node_ref` (a Graph `13 LOAD` node of the LOAD subtype `LAMP` — the Item DB assigns the subtype id, currently `2 LAMP`; the Graph names only `HEATER`; provisional), `base_pm` (from the def's `emits`) and `switch_on`. Its brightness is `lamp_output_pm` (Formulas D.1): `output_pm = switch_on and armed and live ? ⌊base_pm * served_pm / 1000⌋ : 0`. The lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim. **`served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction `sat_k`, independent of the node's own request** (Graph D.6), so a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000: the Emitter's own `switch_on` is the gate, not the Graph, or an off lamp would shine. Power draw is a Graph LOAD: inside the `set_switch` apply the Emitter calls M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` with `req_w` the def's rated draw (Graph MVP: 20 W) when on and 0 when off (Class B: it clamps to `0..req_max`, queues to the next Graph phase 0, and is a no-op on an unknown, tombstoned, dormant or SALVAGED node). A lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (Graph P1); under re-energise inrush the bank draws `req_w * INRUSH_PM / 1000` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs, which can dim the tier-3 bank for half a second — the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip, changing no Emitter rule. The Emitter never recomputes watts and never calls M14 for node lanterns or the beam. A FIXTURE with `node_ref` 0 is *self-powered*: permitted only for the two declared subkinds, EMERGENCY (the cryo-bay emergency lamp, exactly one in the world, declared by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`) and DOCK_STATUS (below); it has no M14 call, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`, and any other `node_ref` 0 fixture is refused by the authoring lint and at boot (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`: exactly one EMERGENCY, exactly one DOCK_STATUS per dock room, none elsewhere). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; second subkind added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* **The DOCK_STATUS fixture (user ruling X2, 2026-10-27)** keeps the pod console's lit gate satisfied at every dock without a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (Interaction's IA-6 refusal of a `pod_hop` exemption stands): it is an *ordinary lit fixture* (`gates_actions` true, SOFT curve, counted in `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `section_emission`, so the web can read it like any lamp, P3 and "light is never free"), authored by Derelict Authoring on the dock room's docked-podcraft prop, in the **dock room's section** and not on the pod body (the pod section is dormant always, Web Map WM-5, and the lamp must not depend on it). It is created and discarded with its section (E1, E2), has no `node_ref` and therefore no liveness test (EM-13 concerns Graph nodes) and cannot be failed, starved or drained by any ship state, which is the point: the stranded player always finds the console lit. Its `switch_on` is driven only by the mutator **E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)`**, which Web Map & Transit calls in the apply that writes `pod_at` (on for the dock room the pod parks at, off for the one it leaves; the berth and unberth verbs are the derelict weld verbs and have nothing to do with it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft named the berth and unberth applies, and read `pod_at` at E1)*, so the glow emits only while the pod is there. **E1 creates every DOCK_STATUS glow switched off and reads nothing of Web Map's state**: E1 runs at `init_world` step 2, before Web Map writes `pod_at` at step 7, so the home dock's glow is switched on by Web Map's step-7 call to E10 (`pod_at` HOME) in the same `init_world` apply, and the derelict docks' glows stay off until the pod parks there. `set_switch` of either origin is refused `NOT_SWITCHABLE` for this subkind and Interaction registers no switch interactable for it; it takes no M14 call and no ARMING, and E10 has no commit-spacing guard and writes no `last_toggle_tick` (E10's row in EM-5 gives the reason: the pod's own timing spaces the transitions, and an atomic apply could not observe a refusal) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Values** (placeholders, owner game-designer and art-director, confirmed by the Lighting spike; derivation in D.1b): `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48, shape row 7 (`FIXTURE`, SOFT) at that reach, and the placement constraint `DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` 24 (the console subject's anchor lies within 24 px of the glow origin, clear of every occluder). Its luminance and hue sit outside the visible-unknown lamp's band (the art-director's, not this GDD's; a Lighting `hue_class` token owed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
215	
216	**EM-12 — One latency story for switching.** A `set_switch` applies at P2 of tick `T_a`; its M14 call is queued to the next Graph phase 0; the lamp is **ARMING with `output_pm` 0** until `arm_tick`, the first `graph.propagate.power` run that consumed the request, and is lit on the first `emitter.place` at or after it (Formulas D.2 `switch_latency`: `arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`). Under the stated assumptions the lamp is lit between 0 and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after the apply — at most 83 ms — and no single number from this paragraph is a design fact: D.2 derives the range with a worked example at both alignments (switch on a Graph tick; switch on the tick after one). **Assumption A1 (derived, not assumed; confirmed by the Graph 2026-10-27 in its Interactions row for this system):** kernel CR-2 ("P3 sees all of P2") and Graph LS-8 phase 0 ("apply queued unconditional inputs: `set_load_request` changes") together mean that an M14 call made in P2 of a Graph tick is consumed by that same tick's phase 0, so the range is 0..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks; the negative case, a Graph that applied only strictly later requests, would give 1..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and is kept in D.2 as the labelled alternative. The direct `after: graph.propagate.failure` entry (EM-1) guarantees that the hook reads that run's output on the same tick. Switching **off** is immediate (`output_pm` 0 from the apply tick; M14 `(node_ref, 0)`); an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels the pending ON and is not a realised transition (it writes no `last_toggle_tick`, EM-7, D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)* The same "light changes only on committed state" rule PC-5 states for the beam holds for fixtures; the asymmetry (ON waits for the Graph pulse, OFF does not) is deliberate and physical: the ship has to serve the lamp, and the lamp cannot go on ahead of the ship. Fixtures never pre-play light; the wall-switch click and animation pre-play. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
217	
218	**EM-13 — Liveness: a lamp is dark when its node is dead.** A lamp or lantern is *live* iff its `node_ref` exists and `node(id).state` is neither `3 DESTROYED`, `2 FAILED`, `4 SALVAGED` nor `5 ABSENT` (Graph LS-10) and the node is not dormant or tombstoned (read each tick from the Graph read view). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 'live' is the output rule only. Command validation uses 'structurally present' (EM-7), which excludes SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant and tombstoned nodes but not FAILED or DESTROYED ones, so a failed lamp can still be switched.)* A not-live lamp has `output_pm` 0 while its `switch_on` stays as committed — when the node is repaired the lamp lights again without a new command. `served_pm` and node `state` are read live each tick; both change only on Graph ticks, and because `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (EM-1) a Graph-tick read sees the state the run just produced, never a pre-failure-phase state. Which Graph states count as "running" for a *lantern* is the Item DB's `lantern_on_states` (default `{0 OK, 1 DEGRADED}`, resolved 2026-10-26). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(orchestrator ruling: R22 as amended at the checkpoint (CP-3) — `emitter.place` declares the direct `after:` entry, so no read is ever lagged; the technical-director's proposal to sample slow inputs once per Graph run into canonical state is not adopted, because the direct ordering needs no sampled state and a restore at a Graph tick rebuilds the identical table.)*
219	
220	**EM-14 — Node lanterns are derived and switchless.** A NODE_LANTERN stands for the glow of a running machine (every machine node whose def carries an `emits` with shape `LANTERN`; the kinds are Item DB data, IDB-31, not a list in this rule: in the MVP a reactor cell, a coolant pump and a scrubber). E1 creates one NODE_LANTERN per such node, and nothing in this rule restricts the kind; the shape key stays `LANTERN` and the hue is per loop (`LANTERN_POWER`, `LANTERN_COOLANT`, `LANTERN_O2`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* It has no switch and makes no `set_load_request` call: `output_pm` is `⌊base_pm * term / 1000⌋` when the node is live and *running* (Formulas D.3 `node_lantern_output`), where `term` is the node's `run_pm` reading. A lantern gated on `served_pm` alone would glow from a switched-off machine (the same trap as EM-11), so the lantern reads a *running* quantity `run_pm` from the Graph read view — **delivered by the Graph** (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27: `node(id).run_pm`, 0..1000 — 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0), otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; it is not the Graph's D.9 `duty_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier and carries the same trap as EM-11). The Emitter **consumes `run_pm` as published and clamps it** to 0..1000 (D.3): it never recomputes it from `out_w`, so a REACTOR running above rated output cannot make a lantern outshine its `base_pm`, and a rated output of 0 is the Graph's guard, not an Emitter division. There is no fallback form: a browned-out or starved machine glows at its served fraction and a lantern that cannot read `run_pm` is a boot defect, not a weaker rule (a lantern at full `base_pm` while its machine starves would lie about power state, P1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Lanterns are created and destroyed with their section (EM-5), counted against Lighting's lantern budget by authoring lint (EM-26), and killing the machine is the only way to dark one — "every loop you run is a lantern the web can see" (art bible Principle 3).
221	
222	**EM-15 — Deployables and glowsticks: spawn on landing, steady, then waning, then gone.** `spawn_deployable(kind, pos_px, owner, life_ticks)` (E3) is called by Interaction's landing-tick hook (PC D.16: "the light exists only on landing"; the thrown light is never pre-played). Sections are never point-sampled; they aggregate by emitter list (`section_emission`, EM-27). `moving` is a per-registration flag: ACTOR and HORROR subjects are always moving; an ITEM registers static (a carried item is unregistered at pickup and re-registered at drop); only moving registrations count against `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`. **The owner stands in their own light** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's SD-7 adopted with the checkpoint fix CP-9 — as first proposed it excluded the owner's beam from the owner's lux, so a player alone with the lamp on would have read `lux` 0 to Horror, the opposite of P3)*: the owner's own beam contributes its **full `output_pm`** — the d = 0 apex value, which EM-19 already places inside every cone — to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and of occlusion, so the owner's self-lux never flips with the way they face; it is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm` (the player is never the target of their own verb for the `act_gate` lit test; the one self-targeted verb, the ACTOR_SELF self-patch, is `act_gate`-exempt, Interaction IA-6, so `lit(ACTOR_SELF)` is never consulted for it and no self-lit or anchor-coverage rule is owed here; crediting the owner's beam to `act_lux_pm` is deliberately not done) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Attention reads the beam as *emission* (`emitters()`, `section_emission`) and does not add the same beam again to the owner's lux (EM-27). Every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary cone test. **An unregistered ref answers exactly like an unlit registered one** *(orchestrator ruling: SD-16 adopted — a P4 requirement)*: `lux(ref)` is 0 and `lit(ref)` is false in release builds, so the Perception Filter's phantom targets (kernel Open Question 14) cost Interaction the same check as real unlit ones and the query cannot become an existence oracle that undermines the phantom-loot hallucination. A debug-only `registered(ref)` exists for tests and the Debug Overlay. Registration over `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` returns false, increments `emitter_subjects_overflow` and the subject reads dark (fails safe); a duplicate registration is a no-op returning false. **Runtime overflow is a content or budget defect, never a gameplay state** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 3)*: failing safe to dark is the right behaviour for a subject the table cannot hold, but a real object sitting visibly inside a beam that refuses to prompt breaks design test 1 (the honest edge) and the P4 "reach for it" falsifier, because the player reads a real lit object as a hallucination. So the caps are held upstream by budgets, not discovered at run time (EM-24, D.15 I-CAPS (d)), and the two counters `emitter_subjects_overflow` and `emitter_moving_overflow` ship in release builds as telemetry (the probe counter went with the probes, EM-24) (a counter in the diagnostics block, not only a debug assertion), so a budget breach in a playtest or live build is visible and reportable. The subject table fields are below; every subject's `body_id` is derived (Layout `body_of(section_id)`; Body `body_of_actor` for an ACTOR) and never stored or hashed *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. 250	**EM-22 — `lit(subject)`: threshold, hysteresis and the beacon exception.** `lit(ref)` is a hysteresis filter over `act_lux_pm` (Formulas D.8): it becomes true when `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, becomes false when `act_lux_pm < LIT_OFF_PM`, and holds between. Placeholders `LIT_ON_PM` 150 (range 100–300) and `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 (60–140), the `LIT_THRESHOLD_PM` family **owned by the technical-artist** (art bible 7.0: "the illumination threshold that enables prompt and inspect-card drawing"), confirmed against the rendered edge in the Lighting spike (8.12 step 2). A newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place`. A hard-edged rim is a *step* (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel), which the 150/120 hysteresis never sees; rim chatter while a beam sweeps is held by the Controller's committed-aim quantisation (`AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` 32 units) and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6), and the hysteresis bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning glowsticks, fixture pools). There is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0): keeping `lit` true after the light went would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie. `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` are separate answers because the beacon's sweep must not strobe prompts (EM-16). **The hysteresis bit is canonical** (checkpoint ruling CP-2): `lit(ref)` depends on last tick's answer, and a subject whose `act_lux_pm` sits between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` has no other source for its bit, so by EM-4's own definition the bit is a discrete fact — one bit per registered subject, at most `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` bits, snapshotted and hashed. `post_restore` rebuilds `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored emitters and **keeps the bit**; the next `emitter.place` applies hysteresis normally. A subject saved at 130 permille and lit is therefore lit after the restore, and Interaction's `validate` at T+1 reads the same answer in the live run and the restored run (kernel G4). *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's canonical bitset is the rule. Rejected alternative: rebuild every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` in `post_restore` (the earlier ruling R6) — a subject between the thresholds would flip from lit to unlit across a restore, `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other, and canonical state downstream would diverge.)* Interaction's `validate` and the HUD prompt call this same `lit(ref)`, so the prompt never lies by omission (PC-6).

252	**EM-23 — The order of work inside `emitter.place`; static and dynamic layers; no subscriptions.** The hook does, in this order and nothing else: **W0** read upstream (`controller.state` and `body.state` for bound seats; the Layout `OccluderSource.version(section_id)`; the Graph's `served_pm` and `node(id)`; on Graph ticks the Graph's `failures(filter)`), and rewrite the derived `section_id` and `body_id` of each BEAM record and ACTOR subject from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)` (a tick in which the foot crosses a door moves the beam's section in that tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, AND, for every loaded section whose Layout `static_version(section_id)` differs from the value cached at the last W0 (a derived per-section cache, never hashed, reset in `post_restore` so the first W0 after a restore re-reads everything), re-read `body_of(section_id)` and `section_offset(section_id)` and rewrite the derived `body_id` of every record and non-ACTOR subject whose `section_id` is that section (cost `W_FRAME` each, D.14); a change of `body_id` or `section_offset` is a FRAME CHANGE of that section *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; **W1** lifecycle (DEAD force-off, deployable aging, evict-wane (D.9b) and removal, `arm_tick` arming, fault-glow reconciliation); **W2** derive every emitter in ascending id (origin, aim, reach, `output_pm`, record `lit`); **W3** find the static-layer rows whose inputs changed; **W4** update them by deltas, in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), **synchronously — nothing is left pending past W4** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **W5** the dynamic layer for every subject (with the owner-beam special case of EM-21: the owner's own beam adds its apex value to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` with no cone or occlusion test); **W6** saturating sums, hysteresis, write the subject table, record the tick's counted work; **W7** write dirty keys (EM-26). The **static layer** (FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW, resting DEPLOYABLE) is cached as **per-pair contribution rows** `(emitter id, subject ref) → {d, f_pm, c}` (a row exists only while the emitter is in radius and unblocked) plus, per subject, an **unsaturated** raw sum `Σ c`, clamped to 1000 only when the answer is read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The first draft cached a saturated partial sum, which is exact for *adding* an emitter (`min(1000, min(1000, a) + b) = min(1000, a + b)`) but cannot *remove* one (a saturated 1000 has forgotten what it summed), so every output change would have forced a full re-evaluation of the subject; with the pair rows every change is a delta: (i) an emitter's **output** changes (to or from 0, a brownout step, inrush): `c = ⌊output_pm × f_pm / 1000⌋` is recomputed from the stored `f_pm` with no geometry, and an `output_pm` of 0 stores `c` = 0 with no multiply while the rows (the geometry) are kept, so a blackout is a zeroing of rows and not a re-evaluation of the ship, and switching back on is a delta too; (ii) an emitter's integer **reach** changes (a waning stick): `d` and `f_pm` are recomputed for its rows and rows beyond the new reach are dropped, with no occlusion test (reach only shrinks, so no pair is added); (iii) an emitter is **created** (its candidate subjects are tested radius first, then occlusion, and rows are added) or **removed** (its rows are dropped); (iv) a subject is **registered or moved** (it is tested against the static emitters in range); (v) an **occluder** changes (only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested, below); (vi) the layer is **cold** (`post_restore`, section instantiate: everything is built); (vii) a **FRAME CHANGE** (a weld or cut, Layout LY-16 / LY-17) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rows store `d`, `f_pm` and `c` and no coordinates, and a weld or cut moves a whole body by one translation (`rot_q` is 0 in the MVP, Layout D.6 / D.12), so: (a) rows whose emitter and subject lie in the same moved component are KEPT unchanged; (b) rows whose emitter `body_id` differs from the subject `body_id` after re-derivation are DROPPED (a cut: the rows that crossed the severed seam; cost `W_DELTA` each); (c) every subject with a changed `body_id` or on the host side of the seam is tested radius-first against the emitters of the OTHER side that are now on its body, and rows are ADDED (a weld; cost `U_sub` with the cross-seam counts of S8); (d) for each socket-host section the hatch slot set changed (PLATE <-> JAMB + LEAF), so pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested exactly as for a leaf change (narrowing rule L / D). Layout reports the kind of change per section as `changed_region(section_id)` = ALL, REGION(box) or FRAME: FRAME = translation only, no re-test; REGION = the socket slot union box (a socket-host section that also moves reports REGION, and the Emitter detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value); ALL (build, discard, restore, or attach / detach if Layout declines REGION / FRAME) = cold rebuild of the affected bodies, priced as S8b. The rebuild stays synchronous (W3 / W4); nothing is pending past W4. Rows are derived, never hashed, rebuilt in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), and sized by ADR candidate 4; a row-table overflow changes cost, never an answer, and increments `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`; the **dynamic layer** (BEAM, BEACON, which rotate or translate every tick) is recomputed per tick with the cheapest rejects first — radius, then cone, then the occlusion test. A subject's static rows are updated when `emitter.place` *observes* a change in what it read last tick: the section's `OccluderSource.version(...)` changed, an emitter's `output_pm` or integer `reach_px` changed, an emitter was created or removed, or the subject moved. **Never by subscription**: kernel CR-10 ("simulation systems never subscribe; sim-to-sim is ordered step reads or commands"); dirty keys are the notification channel for PRESENTATION and friends, not an input to this block. A pose-unchanged skip (a dynamic emitter whose origin, aim, output, shape and occlusion origin equal last tick's skips re-evaluation) is a pure optimisation and changes no answer. A static emitter's cost is paid when something changes, not every tick; a glowstick's reach steps by one px every 50 ticks while it wanes (3600 ticks over 72 px, D.9), so the rows of the subjects in its range are recomputed that often (D.14, S5). **Narrowing rule for door leaves** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` says only *that* something in the section changed, and a leaf bump arrives at the Graph's step rate while a door travels (roughly ten per second), so a response that re-tests every pair of the section would cost 11,522 units per bump (D.14, S1: 14 × `T_sub` 823) against `B` 10,000 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The Emitter therefore re-tests only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region: **(L)** Layout publishes the changed region with the bump (ask E-N, a union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; a structural bump — build, discard, restore — reports `ALL`; attach and detach report REGION / FRAME (trigger vii) when Layout supplies them, else `ALL`), or, if Layout declines, **(D)** every pair whose segment bounding box meets a door-leaf pre-filter box of its section is tagged *dynamic* and evaluated every tick in the dynamic layer, which costs the same amount every tick instead of once per bump (priced in S1). ADR candidate 4 chooses between L and D on Layout's answer; both fit the budget. A restore-time bump (Layout's `post_restore`, version 1 to 2) is treated as a leaf-region change over that section's leaf boxes, not as `ALL`, because structural geometry is valid straight after `restore()` (Layout LY-26 b). **The contract is "never stale", and the rebuild is synchronous** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the question that D.13's age bound left open)*: W3 and W4 finish every update inside the tick, before W6 writes the table, so there is no pending state and the D.13 bound (age 0 or 1 tick) holds for every reader, including Interaction's `validate` at T−1 and its six-tick re-check, Attention and Horror. A tick whose updates exceed the ceiling of D.14 still completes them, increments `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` and is a hitch to be removed by content or by the ordered fallbacks, never deferred. **Alternative (b), rejected and recorded for ADR candidate 4:** a deterministic counted-unit cap per tick, a widened staleness bound and a fail-safe lit-or-dark rule for pending subjects. It was rejected because (1) `lit` would then depend on a rebuild queue that is derived, not canonical, so a snapshot restored mid-queue (which rebuilds cold and complete) would answer differently from the uninterrupted run — kernel G4 broken in exactly the way the old probe budget broke it (EM-24); (2) a fail-safe-dark rule would blink the prompts of a whole room on every door bump; and (3) it would rewrite the age bound that three designed GDDs already build on. The ceiling's named owner is the technical-director; the exposure spike reports it (AC-53).
