254	**EM-24 — Counted work, not wall-clock; the caps.** The per-tick exposure cost is bounded by **counted work units**, never by timing — a time-based governor would be nondeterministic. The caps (all *placeholder, owner technical-director, confirmed by the exposure spike and the Interaction / Derelict Authoring content counts*; never inherited from a default of 64): `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 (derived from the MVP slice's 14 compartments — home-ship 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 — their verb-bearing nodes, doors counted twice for their two face subjects, loose items, actors and horror subjects; Formulas D.14; *orchestrator pick: the systems-designer's 192 over the technical-director's 128, because doors register two subjects (EM-20 e) and the MVP Graph's node count supports a larger interactable set*), `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16 (the 17th moving registration returns false, increments `emitter_moving_overflow` and the subject reads dark, the same fail-safe as `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`), `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` 4, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` 10. **The caps are content budgets, held at data load, not gameplay states** *(CD-GDD-ALIGN concerns 1 and 3)*: the MVP slice has exactly 8 live faults world-wide, of which a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows (registry `mvp_fault_allocation`); I-CAPS therefore requires `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` to be at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus 25 % (⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8; the cap of 10 keeps 2 of headroom), and requires the **dynamic registrants** that arrive after boot to be held to per-category budgets owned by their authors: Derelict Authoring owns the budget for authored OBJECT and ITEM subjects and for dropped loot and spawned salvage per section, Horror Entities owns the horror-subject budget (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (Horror Entities, registry), all moving; Horror's `horror_subject_count` holds `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` + `A_max` 4 = 6 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`) and the share of `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` it may use, Interaction owns the dropped-item registrations, and the deployable budget is `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` + `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (D.14, D.15 I-CAPS (d)). A runtime overflow of any cap is a defect of one of those budgets, is counted by a release-build telemetry counter (`emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_moving_overflow`, `emitter_fault_glow_overcap`, `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow`, and, added by the 2026-10-27 design review, `emitter_create_refused`, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor`, `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`, `emitter_reach_invalid`, `emitter_actor_section_none`, `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling`, and, added by the re-review, `emitter_dock_status_missing`, `emitter_invalid_transition` and the playtest counters of the metric stub) as well as asserted in debug, and is never something a design relies on. `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS` is **0.4 ms P99** for `emitter.place` plus all exposure evaluation (placeholder, spike on the release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, delegated ruling R12; the kernel's `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold and P3's target is ≤ 2.0 ms P99 with the Graph at 0.5 ms and Controller + Body about 0.3 ms). It is the *steady-state* budget; the named rare-event scenarios of D.14 are held to `EXPOSURE_TICK_CEILING_MS` (hot class) and `COLD_REBUILD_CEILING_MS` (cold class), both owned by the technical-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Mandatory work (the dynamic layer, static rebuilds, the subject table) is never skipped. **Creation at `MAX_EMITTERS`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft had no run-time rule at the global cap)*: when the record count equals `MAX_EMITTERS` a creation is **refused**, never made by removing a light that has a physical cause. E1 refuses the section's remaining records, `spawn_deployable` returns false (the item was already spent, Item DB rule (c)), and a FAULT_GLOW reconciliation creates nothing for the lowest-ranked descriptors; each refusal increments `emitter_create_refused` (release telemetry, per kind) and asserts in debug. Within one pass creations are admitted in `priority` order, highest first (BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60; ties by ascending creation order), so the light the player most needs is the one kept; the seat beams are never refused, because their slots are reserved (I-CAPS (a) counts the bound seats). The cap is a content budget held by I-CAPS (a); the rule exists so that a breach is deterministic, counted and visible, never a gameplay state. **Probes and `lit_by(point)` are deferred to Vertical Slice A** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no MVP consumer calls them (Horror HE-19 and HE-25 use Layout `room_at` / `room_adjacency` and make no `probe()` call, Attention AT-4 makes none, Sanity no longer uses `lit_static` (deferred to VS-A, EM-25), and Interaction's re-checks are `lit(ref)` lookups), so `probe`, `lit_by`, `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK`, `W_PROBE`, `probes_allowed` and the probe counter are removed from the MVP read view, budget and acceptance criteria. The first draft derived `probes_allowed` from the previous tick's counted work `T_mand_prev`, which depends on cache hits and skips, is not canonical (absent from EM-28) and is rebuilt differently after `post_restore`, so the same probe could answer OK in a live run and `UNKNOWN` after a restore — a kernel G4 break that the old AC-54 could not detect. **Reserved for VS-A:** if probes return, their budget is a *constant* number per tick that is never derived from counted work, and their signatures take the frame, `probe(body_id, point)` and `lit_by(body_id, point)`, because geometry is compared only within one body (EM-30). The GDScript op cost is not sourceable from the pinned engine reference (no scripting module), so every cost number is a model parameter for the spike; the fallback if the dynamic layer is too slow is a baked per-room illumination grid for the static layer (the brief's option c), then reducing `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`, then room-gated broadphase (the numeric decision table of D.14 governs the order). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
255	
256	**EM-25 — Query semantics, the read view and the staleness bound.** Public reads are table lookups against the subject table and the emitter records; they are pure, side-effect free and callable from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation prompts, **never from notification handlers that decide state** (kernel C.3 row 7). Because `emitter.place` runs every tick, a reader that does not declare `after: [emitter.place]` sees a value **at most one tick old**; P2 `validate` sees the table committed by tick T-1's `emitter.place`; a hook that declares `after: [emitter.place]` sees the current tick (the routed ruling's correction of the brief's "up to 5 ticks", which was borrowed from the Graph's divisor-6 caveat and does not apply to a divisor-1 hook). Source ages stack on top and are named, not hidden: the beam's committed aim is up to the Controller's tolerance behind the drawn aim; a lamp's brightness follows `served_pm`, which changes only on Graph ticks. Owners of channelled verbs re-check exposure every 6 ticks through the same `lit(ref)` and abort if unlit at a check (PC-7); a single-tick flicker between checks is tolerated. Attention declares `after: [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]` (cross-divisor `after:` is already in use: `controller.step` is `after: suit.vitals`) and Horror Entities declares `after` both Attention and `emitter.place` (kernel row 9; HE-3), so the former asks are met and AC-60 lints them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

A GDScript read that cannot meet "copy-free, read-only, no allocation" as plain `Dictionary` code is why the layout is an ADR and not an implementation choice *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | current if `after: emitter.place`, else ≤ 1 tick |

393	
394	*Conventions. Every quantity is an integer (permille `_pm` 0..1000, base px, ticks, Q14 / Q28 fixed point). Every `⌊a / b⌋` divides non-negative operands (GDScript integer division truncates toward zero, so no formula divides a negative). Names are used verbatim — registry (locked): `TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `AIM_UNITS` 4096, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, and the Graph's `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 and `INRUSH_PM` 1500. 395	
396	### D.1 Lamp output
397	
398	The `lamp_output_pm` formula is defined as:
399	
400	`output_pm = switch_on × armed × live × ⌊ base_pm × served_pm / 1000 ⌋` — the lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim

405	|---|---|---|---|---|
406	| `switch_on` | bool | 0/1 | `emitter.state` | the committed switch (fixture, beacon) |
407	| `armed` | bool | 0/1 | D.2 | `T >= arm_tick` (always 1 for a self-powered FIXTURE, `node_ref` 0) |
408	| `live` | bool | 0/1 | Graph `node(node_ref).state` | node exists, is not dormant or tombstoned, and its state is not `2 FAILED`, `3 DESTROYED`, `4 SALVAGED`, `5 ABSENT` (EM-13) |

414	### D.1b Dock status glow sizing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*

416	The `dock_status_glow` sizing is defined as the set of constraints the self-powered DOCK_STATUS fixture (EM-11) must satisfy, with D.1 and D.7 as the formulas:

418	`output_pm = DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` while `switch_on` (self-powered: `armed` 1, `live` 1, `served_pm` 1000, so D.1 reduces to `base_pm`); the console subject at distance `d_c ≤ DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` from the glow origin is lit iff `c(d_c) = ⌊ DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM × F(d_c, R) / 1000 ⌋ ≥ LIT_ON_PM`, `R = DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX`, `F(d, R) = ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋`

420	**Constraints.** (C1) `R ≥ REACH_MIN_PX` 24 (I-REACH). (C2) the console is lit with margin at the farthest allowed placement: `c(DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX) ≥ LIT_ON_PM` plus a margin that absorbs a placement tolerance. 430	### D.2 Switch latency
431	
432	The `switch_latency` formula is defined as:
433	
434	`arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS − (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, `L = arm_tick − T_a`; the negative case (A1 false, a Graph that consumes only strictly later requests) is `arm_tick′ = T_a + GRAPH_STEP_TICKS − (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`

436	**Variables:**
437	
438	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
439	|---|---|---|---|---|
440	| `T_a` | int | ≥ 0 | kernel clock | the tick whose P2 applies `set_switch` / `set_beacon`; **or the creation tick of an E1 authored-on lamp or beacon** (0 at `init_world`, which runs in LOADING before the first RUNNING tick; the range is widened from ≥ 1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) |
441	| `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int | 6 | registry (locked) | Graph hooks run at divisor 6; under the baseline stagger (LS-8: power 0, atmo 2, failure 4) the power hook, which consumes M14, runs at offset 0, so for input timing a Graph tick is `T mod 6 = 0` (EM-1, terminology) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
442	| `arm_tick` | int | `T_a`..`T_a + 5` | calculated | the first Graph tick whose phase 0 consumes the queued M14 request; the lamp is ARMING (`output_pm` 0) before it |

447	### D.2b Switch commit spacing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32; default applied, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20))*
448	
449	The `switch_commit_spacing` formula is defined as:
450	
451	`accept ⇔ last_toggle_tick < 0 ∨ commit_tick − last_toggle_tick ≥ SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`, with `commit_tick = T_a` for a beam toggle, for an OFF that darkens a lit or armed lamp, and for **every switch of a self-powered `node_ref` 0 fixture** (no M14 call, no ARMING, `armed` always 1: its ON commits at the apply tick, so charging it the `arm_tick` of D.2 would shift its spacing check by 0..5 ticks *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `commit_tick = arm_tick` (D.2) for the ON of a Graph-powered lamp, and no test at all for an OFF applied while the lamp is ARMING (it cancels an ON that never became visible); a rejection is `TOO_SOON` for `toggle_beam` and `COOLDOWN` for `set_switch`
452	
453	**Variables:**
454	
455	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
456	|---|---|---|---|---|
457	| `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` | int | 12 (11–20) | this GDD, placeholder owner technical-director and technical-artist, confirmed by 2D Lighting LO-22 | the least number of commit ticks between two realised switch transitions of one emitter |
458	| `last_toggle_tick` | int | −1 or ≥ 1 | the record (EM-4) | commit tick of the previous realised transition |
459	| `commit_tick` | int | `T_a`..`T_a` + 5 | D.2 | the projected tick at which the requested transition becomes visible (`T_a` exactly for a self-powered fixture) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
460	| `N(s)` | int | — | derived | the most realised transitions of one emitter inside any rolling window of 60 ticks at spacing `s` |
461	
462	**Derivation (the constraint `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` satisfies).** The flash budget is `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 per second, and the registry `flash_count` unit is ⌈n / 2⌉ (X9), so one emitter may realise at most N = 6 transitions in any rolling second (⌈6 / 2⌉ = 3; seven would be four flashes). At spacing `s`, a half-open window of 60 ticks holds at most N(s) = ⌈60 / s⌉ transitions (2D Lighting's governor convention) and a window closed at both ends holds at most ⌊60 / s⌋ + 1. Requiring N ≤ 6: half-open gives 60 / s ≤ 6, `s` ≥ 10; closed gives ⌊60 / s⌋ ≤ 5, `s` ≥ 11. `s` = 12 ships because it satisfies both with a transition of margin under the governor's count (N(12) = 5, ⌈5 / 2⌉ = 3 flashes; the closed count is 6, three flashes) and because it equals Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft added "so a player's tap path is rarely the tighter guard". 463	
464	**Output Range:** accept or reject; at most 5 realised transitions of one emitter in any 60 ticks, hence at most 3 flashes. **Examples (fixture, previous realised OFF at tick 120):** an ON requested at `T_a` 121 has `arm_tick` 126 (D.2: 121 mod 6 = 1, +5) and 126 − 120 = 6 < 12 → `COOLDOWN`; at `T_a` 126 (a Graph tick) `arm_tick` 126 → 6 → `COOLDOWN`; at `T_a` 127 `arm_tick` 132 → 12 → accepted; at 132 `arm_tick` 132 → accepted. **ON then OFF:** ON at 1201 (`arm_tick` 1206, realised at 1206, so `last_toggle_tick` 1206 from then); OFF at 1203 → cancels, accepted, writes nothing; but OFF at 1213 → 1213 − 1206 = 7 → `COOLDOWN`, OFF at 1218 → 12 → accepted. **Beam:** toggles submitted on 60 consecutive ticks T..T + 59 are accepted at T, T + 12, T + 24, T + 36, T + 48, which is 5 accepted and 55 rejected `TOO_SOON` (AC-90). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
465	
466	**ON then the fastest legal OFF (the `12 − L` table)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: an ON applied at `T_a` commits at `arm_tick` = `T_a` + `L` (`L` = D.2, 0..5). The player's next tap may be applied `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 later, at `T_a` + 12, and commits at once. The gap between the two commits is 12 − `L`, so the OFF is refused `COOLDOWN` whenever 12 − `L` < `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` 12, that is whenever `L` > 0, and is accepted only when `L` = 0.

468	| `T_a mod 6` | `L` | ON commits | fastest OFF applies / commits | gap 12 − `L` | OFF result |
469	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
470	| 0 | 0 | `T_a` | `T_a` + 12 | 12 | accepted |
471	| 1 | 5 | `T_a` + 5 | `T_a` + 12 | 7 | `COOLDOWN` |
472	| 2 | 4 | `T_a` + 4 | `T_a` + 12 | 8 | `COOLDOWN` |
473	| 3 | 3 | `T_a` + 3 | `T_a` + 12 | 9 | `COOLDOWN` |
474	| 4 | 2 | `T_a` + 2 | `T_a` + 12 | 10 | `COOLDOWN` |
475	| 5 | 1 | `T_a` + 1 | `T_a` + 12 | 11 | `COOLDOWN` |

477	At the sim a refusal is a domain code (`COOLDOWN`, no HUD text, no light change), so a deliberate off-tap right after an on-tap is refused in 5 of 6 alignments (a tap `L` ticks later, 1 to 5, gets through). The cue itself is Interaction's and the Presenter's to draw (a cross-GDD note). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

779	## Edge Cases
780	
781	**Switching, power and lamps**
782	
783	- **If `set_switch` applies on a Graph tick (`T mod 6 = 0`)**: the lamp is lit by that tick's `emitter.place`; on any other tick it is lit at the next multiple of 6, at most 5 ticks later (D.2). One latency story, no hidden term.
784	- **If a switched-on lamp's `served_pm` is 0 (brownout to zero, SCRAM, shed)**: the lamp is STARVED, `output_pm` 0, `switch_on` unchanged and its request still queued; it lights again with no new command when power returns.
785	- **If a lamp's `output_pm` is at or below `LIT_ON_PM` (a deep brownout, or the 150 permille pump lantern)**: it lights nothing but its own anchor, still adds to sums, and Lighting draws it dim; an honest dim, never a prompt.
786	- **If a lamp's node is SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant or tombstoned (not structurally present)**: M14 is a no-op, `live` is false, `output_pm` is 0, a `SYSTEM`-origin `set_switch` or `set_beacon` is rejected `NOT_LIVE`, a `PLAYER`-origin `set_switch` is accepted and flips `switch_on` (IA-11(a): no node read, no oracle) and the lamp stays dark, and the record stays until its section is discarded. A FAILED or DESTROYED node is different: both origins are accepted (next bullet). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
787	- **If a lamp's node goes FAILED or DESTROYED**: `output_pm` is 0 on that Graph tick (the hook is after the failure phase); `switch_on` is retained, so a repair re-lights the lamp without a command. A `set_switch` of either origin on such a node is accepted (it is structurally present, EM-7) and goes STARVED. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
788	- **If eight lamps are switched on in one tick on a marginal island**: all read the same inrush dip of `served_pm` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs (945 in the D.2 example); ascending-id application makes the result order-free.
789	- **If a lamp is switched off while ARMING**: `switch_on` is false at once, M14 `(node_ref, 0)` is queued and the lamp is never lit; the pending `arm_tick` is discarded.
790	- **If `set_switch` targets a non-FIXTURE (a lantern, the beam)**: rejected `NOT_SWITCHABLE`; no state change and no M14 call.
791	- **If a FIXTURE has `node_ref` 0 and is neither the declared cryo-bay emergency lamp nor a dock room's DOCK_STATUS glow**: the authoring lint and boot refuse it (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`); the declared lamps are armed always, fixed `base_pm`, no M14 (Derelict Authoring is designed: DA-23 declares `fixture_subkind_emergency`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; DOCK_STATUS added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*
792	- **If a dock room has no DOCK_STATUS glow, or two**: the authoring lint refuses it (exactly one per dock room, Derelict Authoring's rule); at run time the pod console would read unlit and `pod_hop` would refuse `NOT_LIT`, which the lint exists to make unreachable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*
793	- **If the pod leaves a dock or parks at one**: Web Map's apply that writes `pod_at` calls E10 off for the dock it leaves and on for the dock it parks at; the glow changes with no ARMING and no commit-spacing guard, so there is no `COOLDOWN` to retry and no case in which a refused call leaves the glow lit over an empty cradle; a call for an unknown section, or one with no glow, is a no-op returning false and counts `emitter_dock_status_missing` (a defect the authoring lint exists to prevent). 795	- **If a lantern's machine is switched off (requested load 0) or starved (breaker open, or served below its request)**: output follows the Graph's `run_pm` clamped to 0..1000 — 0 for a switched-off machine, `base_pm × the served fraction` for a starved or browned-out one; there is no fallback form (D.3). **If a REACTOR reports `run_pm` above 1000** (output above rated): the clamp holds the lantern at `base_pm`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

797	**Beam and pose**
798	
799	- **If `toggle_beam` applies**: `switch_on` flips and the beam is lit on the apply tick; a turn-ON at zero charge is rejected `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the light does not change (the pre-played click is the Presenter's).
800	- **If charge reaches zero mid-channel**: Suit's `force_off` lands before the same tick's `emitter.place`; the owner's 6-tick re-check then finds the target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target.

802	- **If the actor is STAGGERED**: the beam is unchanged and `toggle_beam` is rejected `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (a defensive double of the Controller's input-ignore).
803	- **If the player runs with aim different from facing**: the beam follows the committed aim; the split axes are ±206 units off aim, not facing.
804	- **If an interactable lies between the chest and the feet in screen-y while the player faces up-screen**: it is behind the apex, unlit and unprompted unless it lies within the foot spill: the sim adds no hidden compensation beyond the ruled spill (EM-6). `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` ships at 24 (user ruling D24, 2026-10-27; Open Question 17), so an item within 18 px of the feet is lit and prompts while the beam is on, an item a full tile (48 px) to the side is not, and with the beam off there is no spill; AC-10b tests the ruled default and the spill-off boundary. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

816	- **If a segment only touches a rectangle (corner graze), crosses a seam between abutting rectangles (wall run, door-leaf/jamb joint) or passes through a corner shared by two diagonal rectangles**: it is blocked, because cells are unit squares and abutting boxes share a face (EM-20 a, D.6); an oblique ray never slips through a seam. An evicted glow removes only the light and exposure; the Failure & Trail overlay on the sprite still shows the fault. **If a descriptor's `sev` falls to 0 or its `intensity_pm` ends**: the record is removed on that Graph tick.
835	- **If a long-aged fault (a SCRAM held for minutes) keeps its descriptor while Failure & Trail's overlay decays** (Derelict Authoring OQ-V3): the FAULT_GLOW `output_pm` follows the descriptor's `sev` alone (D.11) and never the overlay's age; overlay decay is Failure & Trail's presentation and changes neither `output_pm` nor exposure, so a glow that should fade with age must be expressed by F&T as a falling `sev` or `intensity_pm`.
836	- **If a `mod_lamp` sits on the lowest `power_tier`** (Derelict Authoring OQ-V4): its output is `base_pm × served_pm / 1000` (D.1); the lowest tier is the first shed under a shortfall, so it reads dimmer only while its tier is under-served (`served_pm` < 1000) and identical to any other lamp at full supply; whether a given `served_pm` reads *visibly* dimmer is the Lighting spike's to confirm.
837	- **If a sprite carries an emissive `_msk` trail glow**: it is an unshaded overlay, not an emitter, and exposes nothing.
838	
839	**Save, restore, boot and co-op**
840	
841	- **If a game is restored with a subject between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM`**: its `lit` bit is canonical and kept, so `validate` at T+1 reads the same answer as in the uninterrupted run (kernel G4).
842	- **If a save is taken at a Graph tick and restored**: the Graph's `post_restore` rebuilds `served_pm` and the descriptor list, so the subject table and every lamp `output_pm` match uninterrupted play at the next five ticks; the Graph now does so (LS-21 and its restore edge case, 2026-10-27), and AC-41 fails if a regression removes the rebuild (lamps would read dark for up to 5 ticks). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
843	- **If a restore completes (the kernel binding table is rebuilt)**: the kernel's LOADING rebuild re-binds the seat beams from `beam_bindings()` before the first RUNNING tick (KRN-BIND-01); there is no window in which `toggle_beam` meets an empty table. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
844	- **If a registrant does not re-register in its own `post_restore`**: nothing is lost (registrations are canonical); a repeat registration is a no-op returning false.
845	- **If a hook id is unknown or creates a cycle at boot** (for example someone registers `after: [emitter.update]`): boot fails loudly (CR-3); only `emitter.place` exists. **If the kernel is FAULTED during a mutator apply**: standard CR-9 handling; every mutator here is Class B or validated, so a fault is a defect.
846	- **If the kernel is `MIRROR`**: it never ticks `emitter.place`; the replica reads `SHARED_SUMMARY`, which in VS-B must carry each beam's origin, aim, shape and switch so a remote crewmate's beam can be drawn.
847	- **If zoom changes**: nothing in the sim changes; an off-screen lit object stays lit and exposes, and the HUD draws no off-screen prompt.
848	
849	**Hallucination and degenerate strategies**
850	
851	- **If the Perception Filter shows a lamp as broken or a dead lamp as working, or adds a decoy light**: `emitter.state` still holds the real `output_pm`, so the room is as lit as it was and the prompt follows the real light; the false lamp is a Lighting visual that exposes nothing, and walking to the real edge is the falsifier.
852	- **If the player (or a replay, a script or a remote submitter) strobes the beam**: every accepted toggle is committed state and visible to Attention, and the sim rejects a toggle applied fewer than `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (12) after the last accepted one with `TOO_SOON` in both directions (EM-7, D.2b), so the beam flips at most five times in a rolling second, at most three flashes (ceil unit), and Lighting's flash governor never has to delay a committed flip; the Adapter's debounce (to be at least 12) still drops the press before it is submitted. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; user rulings: D32)*
853	- **If the player goes dark (beam off, no fixtures)**: `lux_pm` is 0 everywhere except where a self-powered fixture shines (the cryo-bay lamp; a dock room's DOCK_STATUS glow while the pod is parked there, X2), nothing else is lit and no lit-only verb is possible outside those pools; darkness is never free (only `drop`, `toggle_beam`, `throw_glowstick` and the inspect card of an already-lit instrument remain, registry `act_gate`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
854	- **If the player lays glowsticks everywhere or abandons a lit fixture**: each still adds to `section_emission` and Attention's cost, the live cap is 8 and each wanes; light is a spend, never a safe state.
855	- **If Horror wants a light query beyond `lit(ref)`, `lux(ref)` and `emitters_near`**: there is none in the MVP — `probe` and `lit_by` are deferred to VS-A (EM-24), so no consumer can starve the mandatory work through a probe budget. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

948	## Visual/Audio Requirements
949	
950	*This block draws and plays nothing. It publishes facts (the emitter read view, the shape table, dirty keys) that the renderer and the audio mixer conform to; every item below is owned by the GDD named in its row and is listed so that the owner's brief is complete. A sentence that needs `Light2D` to be true belongs to 2D Lighting & Occlusion (undesigned; sibling stage), never to this document.*
951	
952	**What is visible.** Light is the only thing this system shows. A beam is a wedge with a **hard outer edge exactly at its reach** (3 screen px of edge, then a soft interior falloff) in the Tungsten hue every human light uses (art bible 4.2); the four shapes, the fan, the deployable pool, the glowstick, the fixture and the beacon are the art bible 8.3 rows (lines 1079–1086) carried verbatim into the shape table, with two rows this GDD adds (lantern, fault glow) and the HARD / SOFT curve classes owed back to 8.3 (Cross-References). A glowstick is Chemlight `#86B896`, steady and then visibly smaller (art bible 3.2: "steady, then waning"); a fixture never flickers (the cryo-bay lamp's gutter is Lighting's, art bible 8.11 flag 2); the dock status glow is a small, dim, steady fixture whose luminance and hue the art-director keeps apart from the visible-unknown lamp (a Lighting `hue_class` token and the luminance separation are owed by the art-director and art bible 7.0 note; X2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; a node lantern is the glow of a running machine in that loop's own hue at its machinery node (art bible 8.3 emission rule, 8.10 flag 8); fault glows are point sources (ember, power arc, cyan O₂ mist) taken from the Failure & Trail descriptor-to-glow table. Everything is drawn from `emitter.state` and nothing else.
953	
954	**What Lighting reads, and must not do.** Lighting reads the per-emitter read view (`id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, r_off_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority`, AC-46b) and `shapes()`, and it conforms to them: a texture's reach equals `reach_px` ± 1 px for every hard-edged row; a soft pool's boundary is drawn at max(`r_off_px`, `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX`) ± 1 px (D.7, exact sim values), so that the prompt of an already-lit subject ends exactly where the pool visibly ends and an approaching subject meets its prompt `r_off_px − r_lit_px` px inside it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (the sim/render agreement, AC-55 and AC-56, the load-bearing P1 test of the lighting stack); a dimmed emitter is drawn dimmer in proportion to `output_pm` (a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served, Graph D.6). Lighting **owns** the light textures, ambient and `CanvasModulate`, shadow-slot assignment (lint hypotheses: at most 6 shadow-casting, 24 non-shadow and 8 node lanterns in view, art bible 8.10 and 8.11 flags 2 and 8; "emitters are cut before occlusion"), flicker and gutter, the per-light flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling 1 s, pipeline PR-13), and the decoy visuals of the Perception Filter. Lighting **must not**: write an emitter or any block; tell the sim a light is "culled"; give a decoy, a false lamp state or a flicker any query effect (the query reads `output_pm`, not the picture; AC-5a); move the true edge of a real light (art bible Principle 1; the stage-2 "cone seems to reach further" symptom is a **decoy glow past the true edge** with a palette leak, never a wider revealing radius, Cross-References refresh to 4.4); or draw a shadow with no occluder from a horror (actors and horrors never occlude, art bible 3.2, EM-20 c). Occlusion shadows follow the same footprint rectangles the query uses (one source for collision, light and shadow), and the same cell convention: Lighting's occluder polygon for a stored rectangle `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` is the continuous rectangle covering exactly those pixel cells, and an integer position is the centre of its cell (EM-20 a), so a drawn shadow has no seam where the query has none *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the shadow origin versus the sim's foot segment (EM-6, CP-5) is Open Question 5.
955	
956	**What Audio hears.** Audio keys off the `E/<emitter id>` dirty keys (EM-26) and the Presenter's own pre-play, and reads **no exposure** (it does not call `lux` or `lit`). The beam switch click and the wall-switch click pre-play on input (PC-5; the light itself lands on commit); a lamp hum rises across the 0–5 tick switch latency so the warm-up reads as a ship lamp, not lag; a bank switched together draws inrush and the neighbouring dip is a legitimate, audible, player-caused flicker (Graph `INRUSH_PM`); a glowstick may thin a faint chemical hiss as it wanes and ends with a soft quiet; the beacon's sweep has a rotation cadence at `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s); fault glows share their descriptor's audio (Failure & Trail). **Light itself is silent**: this system emits no noise into Attention's intake (noise is a tool property, PC-10).

973	## Game Feel
974	
975	*A real note, not a template fill: this system has no animation, no input of its own and no hit; its feel is the **honesty and timing of light**. The feel of the toggle's input belongs to the Player Controller (PC-5 and its debounce; the sim-side `TOO_SOON` floor beneath it is EM-7), the feel of how light looks to 2D Lighting & Occlusion, the feel of every sound to Audio; this GDD owns the numbers underneath them, which are below.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
976	
977	**Feel reference.** The chest lamp should feel like Pandorum's helmet light and the Alien: Isolation torch in one respect only: it is *yours*, hands-free, always where you are facing, and it is the one thing in the game that never lies. The ship's lamps should feel like a machine that has to be served: they come up with the ship, not ahead of it.
978	
979	**Input responsiveness (beam).** The `toggle_beam` press applies at P2 and the light is committed in the same tick's `emitter.place`: zero internal latency, at most one tick (16.7 ms) from apply to the lit state the renderer sees, inside the Controller's ≤ 17 ms click-to-commit budget (PC-5). The click and the switch animation pre-play; the **light never does** (the Presenter never predicts beam state: the lamp is the human-channel anchor and may not lie for one frame). Turn-off is immediate. Feel target: decisive, mechanical, slightly heavy; never a lag the player reads as the game being slow, never a flash the player reads as the game being wrong.
980	
981	**Ship lamps warm; the chest lamp snaps.** A fixture switched on is ARMING until the Graph serves it: 0 to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` − 1 ticks (0–83 ms), below perception on its own, and Audio's relay clunk and hum rise fill it so it reads as a ship lamp, not as lag. Under a weak bus a bank of lamps switched together draws `INRUSH_PM` 1500 for `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 Graph runs (0.5 s): the neighbouring lamps dip (the Graph example is 945 permille) and recover. That dip is an honest, audible, **player-caused** flicker and the best single lesson the ship teaches about load; it must never be smoothed away.
982	
983	**The rim.** At full output the edge of a HARD emitter is a step (about 252 permille inside, 0 outside; `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` 250 with `LIT_ON_PM` 150), so an object pops into reach at an exact pixel. The 150 / 120 hysteresis never sees that step; it bites only on **dimmed** emitters (brownout, waning glowsticks) whose interior crosses the threshold band, so a prompt does not strobe in a fade. While the aim is sweeping, committed-versus-drawn divergence of up to 2.8° and ≤ 3 ticks (PC-5) moves the rim by about 14 px at 288 px (WIDE) and 19 px at 384 px (NARROW); a rim object may prompt a few ticks late and rim chatter is held by the Controller's `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`, not by this block. The edge-agreement test (design test 1) holds **at rest and for full-output emitters**; a dimmed light's actionable area shrinks honestly (a fixture at 500 permille loses prompts for objects within 22 px of its full-output readable edge (`r_lit` falls from 122 to 100 px): "the junction box at the edge went out of reach when the scrubber drew").
984	
985	**Glowstick wane and beacon.** A glowstick is steady for its first 60 % of life, then shrinks over the rest in visible integer steps; the shrinking pool is the only clock and no number is ever shown. A stick put out by the live cap is never snuffed: it takes the same visible shrink, faster (10 s, D.9b), so the pool still only ever dies by shrinking. The beacon lights a point for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks, so it is *seen* and never gates a prompt (EM-16): nothing strobes at the sweep rate.
986	
987	**The split beam's dark wedge is its identity.** Two cones at ±18° off the aim with a wedge of at least 16° that never closes: the one shape that cannot see straight ahead. It is a loadout personality, not a bug; nobody should "fix" it.
988	
989	**Impact moments.** (1) A brownout takes the corridor lamps down and, when power returns, the corridor beyond is exactly where it was (the world never lied). (2) A glowstick thrown into the next room: the pool blooms Chemlight green on landing, not in flight. (3) A lamp bank clicking on and the whole deck sagging for half a second. (4) The tell: filaments resolving at the cone edge, which needs this stable edge to resolve at.
990	
991	**Feel acceptance.** AC-FEEL (manual, retained screenshots, technical-artist and game-designer sign-off) covers the toggle, the inrush dip, the rim at rest at three zoom rungs, and the glowstick wane. Weight and responsiveness profile: instant for the beam and turn-off, 0–5 ticks for a fixture, 0.5 s for a bank dip, 150 s for a glowstick.
992	
993	## UI Requirements
994	
995	**No UI of its own.** This system draws no HUD element, menu, instrument or world-space marker, and none is permitted: no exposure bar, ring, icon, "light level" or visibility readout, and no marker on a lit or unlit object (P3: shown in the world, never a meter; Attention is likewise a thing the world does). The only gameplay surface that follows from this block is a **prompt that is present or absent**, and its drawing is owned elsewhere. The surfaces below are the readers of this block's answers; each states what it needs and from where.
996	
997	| Information | Display location (owner) | Update frequency | Condition |
998	|---|---|---|---|
999	| Verb prompt for a target | HUD, anchored with `world_to_hud(target)` (pixel-perfect pipeline; Interaction decides the verb) | every presentation frame from the last committed table | drawn iff `lit(ref)`; absent otherwise; the inspect card of an already-lit instrument is the Controller's exception (PC-6) |
1000	| Rejection feedback for a lit-only verb | the failed-action cue (Interaction; `NOT_LIT` is Interaction's reason) | on the rejected command | `lit(ref)` was false at `validate` |
1001	| Beam and tool charge reading | the suit HUD gauge (Suit & Equipment; art bible HUD set, 7.0) | Suit's divisor-6 vitals | the charge belongs to Suit; this block supplies only `emitter.state.lit` on the beam to drain it |
1002	| Beam shape and toggle state | the tool-readout surface (Suit loadout; Controller draws the hand animation) | on `bind_beam` and on commit | the shape is loadout, never input (EM-8); the lamp itself is the readout |
1003	| Debug Overlay | developer overlay (DIAGNOSTIC subscriber; absent from release) | per frame | cones, occlusion segments and origins, subject `lux_pm` and `lit`, `unknown_subject_queries`, `emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_moving_overflow`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

1005	*Requirements placed on the owners (not drawn here).* The HUD and Interaction never draw a prompt where `lit(subject)` is false, **including for a phantom salvage target** (kernel Open Question 14; an unregistered ref answers like an unlit one, EM-21), because "reach for it" is only a falsifier if the prompt follows the true edge. The prompt must not flicker faster than the Controller's focus stickiness allows (hysteresis is this block's, rim stickiness the Controller's). The inspect card appears only on a lit instrument. Accessibility: nothing about exposure is conveyed by colour alone (there is no exposure display); the edge must read in greyscale (art bible 4.5); a strobe of the chest lamp is bounded by the Adapter's debounce for the local player and by this block's `TOO_SOON` guard for every submitter (EM-7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
1006	
1007	No UX Flag is raised: there is no screen or HUD element of this system to specify with `/ux-design`. The prompt, the failed-action cue and the charge gauge are specified in the HUD, Interaction and Suit UX work (`design/ux/hud.md`; none yet exists), which cite this table.

Brackets name the rule or formula covered. Criteria whose counterpart is undesigned are marked "(provisional — <system> undesigned)" and are not BLOCKING until it lands.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Spike-tagged criteria** (`(spike)`: AC-53, AC-55 to AC-57) are neither BLOCKING nor ADVISORY while their spike has not run: each is reported **NOT ASSESSED** (never passed, never failed) by `/gate-check` and `/smoke-check`, names its spike story and pass line, and becomes BLOCKING the day the spike reports (EM-SPIKE-1 for AC-53, the Lighting spike for AC-55 to AC-57). **Debug assertions are not observable headless**: wherever a criterion says a debug build "asserts", the test observes the assertion through the Diagnostics seam (`FakeDiagnostics.assert_reports`, a list of codes), because a real `assert()` would halt the headless runner and is stripped from Release exports.

findings.fix: State once in EM-7 that the Emitter registers binding_source(ctx) for beam_bindings, delivering ascending (player_id, beam_id) via ctx.put and ending in ctx.complete(). findings.finding: Four sites say the DEAD-tick forced beam-off is 'unobservable in the MVP' because Save/Load calls request_restore at that tick's P6. Under delegated rulings R13/R14, Save/Load stages the epoch write first. Save/Load row 2b says the kernel stays RUNNING with the seat DEAD and the hard gate closed until EPOCH_DURABLE, up to RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS 500 ms = 30 ticks. The forced off is therefore observable for 1-30 ticks, and request_restore is not at that tick's P6.
findings.fix: Replace 'unobservable' with 'held for the epoch-staging window (1 to 30 ticks) before the restore'. Cite SL step 2b. Keep AC-13c, and add that the beam stays off and toggle_beam stays NOT_ACTIONABLE while DEAD persists.

findings.finding: EM-28 claims save-equivalence 'with no accepted exception'. The same paragraph says the cold static build is correct for open doors only if Layout's post_restore runs first. Kernel CR-8 (and its AC at L977) guarantees only that every restore precedes every post_restore, not the order between post_restore calls. The fallback (a version bump re-testing leaf pairs on tick 1) does not say it lands before the first P2 validate. MVP death restarts from autosave, so this is on the main path.
findings.fix: Make the Emitter independent of the order. In post_restore, read Layout's pure leaf-geometry derivation (door_leaf_gap) for the leaf rectangles it needs, instead of relying on Layout's cache. Or ask the kernel to order post_restore by restore_after (G1: the kernel owns it). Reword EM-28 to name whichever mechanism is chosen, and add an AC with a door that is open in the snapshot.

findings.section: EM-7 beam_bindings(), EM-5 E9, AC-15b, AC-112, Interactions row 1
findings.finding: The GDD has zero mentions of ctx. It defines the kernel binding source as 'beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]', a pure read returning a list. Kernel CR-8 and CR-7 (G1: the kernel owns the contract) define binding_source(ctx), delivering [(player_id, entity_id)] through ctx.put and ending 'return ctx.complete()'. A source that returns without the sentinel faults LOADING. AC-15b and AC-112 assert on the returned list. Ruling R3 says no owner callable may be '-> void' or sentinel-less. (Body's seat_bindings() has the same wording.)
findings.fix: State once in EM-7 that the Emitter registers binding_source(ctx) for beam_bindings, delivering ascending (player_id, beam_id) via ctx.put and ending in ctx.complete(). Reword AC-15b and AC-112 to read the delivered pairs, and add a one-line statement that every Emitter owner callable (validate, apply, hook, snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, read_view) follows the CR-19 ctx contract.

findings.section: EM-9 (L210), States and Transitions DEAD row (L324), Edge Cases (L801), Cross-References (L1025), AC-13c
findings.finding: Four sites say the DEAD-tick forced beam-off is 'unobservable in the MVP' because Save/Load calls request_restore at that tick's P6. Under delegated rulings R13/R14, Save/Load stages the epoch write first. Save/Load row 2b says the kernel stays RUNNING with the seat DEAD and the hard gate closed until EPOCH_DURABLE, up to RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS 500 ms = 30 ticks. The forced off is therefore observable for 1-30 ticks, and request_restore is not at that tick's P6.
findings.fix: Replace 'unobservable' with 'held for the epoch-staging window (1 to 30 ticks) before the restore'. Cite SL step 2b. Keep AC-13c, and add that the beam stays off and toggle_beam stays NOT_ACTIONABLE while DEAD persists.

findings.finding: EM-28 claims save-equivalence 'with no accepted exception'. The same paragraph says the cold static build is correct for open doors only if Layout's post_restore runs first. Kernel CR-8 (and its AC at L977) guarantees only that every restore precedes every post_restore, not the order between post_restore calls. The fallback (a version bump re-testing leaf pairs on tick 1) does not say it lands before the first P2 validate. MVP death restarts from autosave, so this is on the main path.
findings.fix: Make the Emitter independent of the order. In post_restore, read Layout's pure leaf-geometry derivation (door_leaf_gap) for the leaf rectangles it needs, instead of relying on Layout's cache. Or ask the kernel to order post_restore by restore_after (G1: the kernel owns it). Reword EM-28 to name whichever mechanism is chosen, and add an AC with a door that is open in the snapshot.

findings.section: States and Transitions (L294-299, L308), AC-109, AC-116
findings.finding: Two lifecycle gaps remain under the rule 'every pair not listed is invalid and reported'. (1) The ON row's 'Who may cause them' omits E10 set_dock_status off, though the OFF row lists it. (2) There is no ABSENT -> STARVED entry. A NODE_LANTERN created at init_world on an idle machine (run_pm 0) has output 0, and so does a FIXTURE created on a dead node. Read literally, E1 fires emitter_invalid_transition for every such lantern, and the lantern would not be created. AC-116 requires that counter to stay at 0.
findings.fix: Add E10 to the ON row. Add a creation row 'ABSENT -> STARVED (NODE_LANTERN whose machine is not running, FIXTURE or BEACON on a not-live node)' to both tables.

findings.finding: Quote: 'GIVEN an emitter in WANING and a command that would move it to OFF, or any transition not listed ... THEN the state is unchanged, emitter_invalid_transition increments by 1'. No public command can reach an unlisted transition. set_switch on a deployable is rejected NOT_SWITCHABLE at validate, so the criterion cannot fail through the public surface.
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'GIVEN the transition-table function exposed to the test build (EM_TEST seam), WHEN it is called with each (from,to) pair not in the tables (exhaustive over the 6x6 state matrix), THEN it returns REJECT, leaves the record unchanged and increments emitter_invalid_transition once, labelled from/to; WHEN called with each listed pair, THEN it returns APPLY and the counter is 0.'

findings.section: EM-4 base_pm row, D.1 base_pm source, Tuning Knobs FIXTURE_BASE_PM, E1
findings.finding: Ruling R7 and Derelict Authoring DA-31/DA-35/AC-DA-46 author fx_corr_1 and fx_corr_2 at base_pm 750 as a placement value (the E1 placement schema carries base_pm). EM-4 defines base_pm only 'from the module def's emits, bind_beam, or BEAM_BASE_PM', and D.1 cites only Item DB emits.base_pm. An implementer of E1 cannot tell whether the placement's 750 or the def's 1000 wins. The 24 px PD-1 bound depends on 750 (r_draw 120, I verified: c(120) = 124 and c(121) = 119 at output 750).
findings.fix: Add the precedence to EM-4, E1 and D.1: a placement base_pm, when present, overrides the def's emits.base_pm. A data lint requires 1 <= placement <= def base_pm. The record stores the placement value. Add an AC (E1 with placement 750 gives output_pm 750 at served_pm 1000 and r_off_px 120).
